attributes.description:
The categories of each feature determined during ``fit`` (in order of
the features in X and corresponding with the output of ``transform``).
This does not include categories that weren't seen during ``fit``.
attributes.name: categories_

attributes.description:
Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.

.. versionadded:: 1.0
attributes.name: n_features_in_

attributes.description:
Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
has feature names that are all strings.

.. versionadded:: 1.0
attributes.name: feature_names_in_

attributes.description:
Defined only if infrequent categories are enabled by setting
`min_frequency` or `max_categories` to a non-default value.
`infrequent_categories_[i]` are the infrequent categories for feature
`i`. If the feature `i` has no infrequent categories
`infrequent_categories_[i]` is None.

.. versionadded:: 1.3
attributes.name: infrequent_categories_

methods.summary: Fit to data, then transform it.

methods.name: get_feature_names_out
methods.summary: Get output feature names for transformation.

methods.name: get_metadata_routing
methods.summary: Get metadata routing of this object.

methods.summary: Convert the data back to the original representation.

methods.summary: Set the parameters of this estimator.

parameters.description:
Categories (unique values) per feature:

- 'auto' : Determine categories automatically from the training data.
- list : ``categories[i]`` holds the categories expected in the ith
  column. The passed categories should not mix strings and numeric
  values, and should be sorted in case of numeric values.

The used categories can be found in the ``categories_`` attribute.
parameters.name: categories
parameters.type_doc: 'auto' or a list of array-like, default='auto'

parameters.description:
When set to 'error' an error will be raised in case an unknown
categorical feature is present during transform. When set to
'use_encoded_value', the encoded value of unknown categories will be
set to the value given for the parameter `unknown_value`. In
:meth:`inverse_transform`, an unknown category will be denoted as None.

.. versionadded:: 0.24
parameters.name: handle_unknown

parameters.description:
When the parameter handle_unknown is set to 'use_encoded_value', this
parameter is required and will set the encoded value of unknown
categories. It has to be distinct from the values used to encode any of
the categories in `fit`. If set to np.nan, the `dtype` parameter must
be a float dtype.

.. versionadded:: 0.24
parameters.name: unknown_value

parameters.description:
Encoded value of missing categories. If set to `np.nan`, then the `dtype`
parameter must be a float dtype.

.. versionadded:: 1.1
parameters.name: encoded_missing_value

parameters.description:
Specifies the minimum frequency below which a category will be
considered infrequent.

- If `int`, categories with a smaller cardinality will be considered
  infrequent.

- If `float`, categories with a smaller cardinality than
  `min_frequency * n_samples`  will be considered infrequent.

.. versionadded:: 1.3
    Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <encoder_infrequent_categories>`.
parameters.name: min_frequency

parameters.description:
Specifies an upper limit to the number of output categories for each input
feature when considering infrequent categories. If there are infrequent
categories, `max_categories` includes the category representing the
infrequent categories along with the frequent categories. If `None`,
there is no limit to the number of output features.

`max_categories` do **not** take into account missing or unknown
categories. Setting `unknown_value` or `encoded_missing_value` to an
integer will increase the number of unique integer codes by one each.
This can result in up to `max_categories + 2` integer codes.

.. versionadded:: 1.3
    Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <encoder_infrequent_categories>`.
parameters.name: max_categories

signature: OrdinalEncoder(*, categories='auto', dtype=<class 'numpy.float64'>, handle_unknown='error', unknown_value=None, encoded_missing_value=nan, min_frequency=None, max_categories=None)
summary: Encode categorical features as an integer array.
